conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate and reduce concentration.
Trim CRWD to 8% to take some profit and reduce concentration.
Reduce SOXL to 1% and sell SPAL to zero to lower overall leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy TECS at 4% and SQQQ at 3% to add exposure to strong scanner long setups.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by blending broad index, quality tech, and a small amount of new leveraged exposure. It reduces overall concentration and leverage from current levels. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a focus on risk-first growth.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate and free up capital.
Trim CRWD to 8% to take some profit and reallocate.
Buy TECS at 6%, SQQQ at 6%, and SOXS at 6% to lean into high-scoring scanner long setups.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to stretch for growth.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by concentrating in high-scoring scanner setups and utilizing leveraged ETFs. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily and can lose a lot quickly; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, PLTU, MUU, METU, MSFU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index exposure. It aims for low drawdown and reliable distributions, but these are variable and NAV can still fall. This is for cash-like income, not a savings account.
